draft.title: Groups and periods
card: A group is a column of the periodic table. Elements in the same group have similar properties.
A period is a row of the periodic table. Moving across a period, the properties change step by step.
The periodic table has 18 groups. Group 1 holds very reactive metals such as lithium, sodium and potassium.
An element's place in the table lets us predict its properties. If we know how sodium reacts, we can expect potassium, in the same group, to react in a similar way.
draft.remember: Groups are columns with similar elements. Periods are rows.

a.q: Lithium and sodium are in the same group. What does this tell us?
opts: They have similar properties
They have exactly the same properties
They are in the same row
They are both non-metals
a.why: Elements in a group are similar, so we can predict one from the other. They are not identical, and a group is a column, not a row.
a.clue: Think about what a column tells you.

b.q: Tom reads that rubidium is in Group 1, below potassium. A teacher asks him to predict how it reacts. What is the best prediction?
opts: It is a reactive metal like potassium
It is an unreactive non-metal
It reacts exactly like potassium
It is in the same period as potassium
b.why: Group 1 elements are very reactive metals, so rubidium should be similar to potassium. It is not identical. Elements in a group are in different periods.

wants.brief: A simple periodic table outline with one column shaded and labelled group, and one row shaded and labelled period.
wants.why: It shows students which direction is a group and which is a period.

b.best: It is a reactive metal like potassium

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'Group 1 elements are very reactive metals', but hydrogen is usually placed in Group 1 and is not a metal. The card is more careful ('holds very reactive metals such as...'). Better: 'Rubidium, like potassium, is a very reactive Group 1 metal.'
